task_2.title: Add default support for Clang 21 settings
task_2.description: The upgrade adds Clang 21 to the library's built-in compiler settings so users can select it without maintaining custom settings definitions. This expands supported toolchain configuration while leaving the existing default C++ standard behavior unchanged.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the built-in compiler settings accept Clang 21 as a valid compiler version so users can configure and consume that toolchain without custom settings overrides, while preserving existing default C++ standard behavior.

expectation.grounded: The default `settings.yml` content must include `compiler=clang` with version `21` as an allowed value. Configurations, profiles, or package settings that use the default settings model and specify Clang 21 should be treated as valid instead of being rejected as an unknown compiler version. The upgrade must not otherwise change the available Clang `cppstd` values or introduce a different default C++ standard behavior for this release.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to declare Clang 21 with the library's standard compiler settings out of the box. Upgrading should expand recognized compiler coverage without changing the expected default language-standard behavior.

constraints.grounded: Existing supported Clang versions must remain valid. The change is limited to recognizing version 21 in the built-in Clang version list and must not remove or alter existing `libcxx`, `runtime`, or `cppstd` setting options for Clang.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should be additive and backward-compatible for existing compiler configurations. It must not silently change unrelated compiler-setting behavior while adding support for the new version.

behavior: The built-in compiler settings model recognizes `clang` version `21` as a valid compiler version.
User configurations that rely on the default settings definitions can select Clang 21 without requiring a custom settings file entry.
The upgrade does not expand or change the default C++ standard options or default-standard behavior as part of adding Clang 21 support.
acceptance_criteria: When a user configures the library with `compiler=clang` and `compiler.version=21` using the default settings definitions, it should accept that configuration as valid.
When a user upgrades from 2.19.1 to 2.20.0, previously supported Clang versions should continue to be accepted unchanged.
When users adopt Clang 21 after the upgrade, they should not observe a newly introduced default C++ standard behavior change attributable to this feature.

task_1.title: Add a built-in minimum compiler version validator for recipes
task_1.description: Conan 2.20.0 introduces a public validator that lets recipes declare minimum supported compiler versions in a concise, standardized way. The validator enforces the minimum version for the active compiler, reports a clearer invalid-configuration error that includes the reason for the restriction, and fails explicitly when compiler settings are unavailable.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan recipes can declare minimum supported compiler versions through a built-in validator and that package consumers receive consistent validation failures when their compiler is too old or compiler metadata is missing.

expectation.grounded: Provide a public `conan.tools.build.check_min_compiler_version(conanfile, compiler_restrictions)` helper for use from recipe validation logic. The helper should accept compiler restrictions as tuples of compiler name, minimum version, and user-facing reason; read `settings.compiler` and `settings.compiler.version`; compare the active compiler version against the matching declared minimum; raise `ConanInvalidConfiguration` when the active compiler is below the declared minimum; and raise `ConanException` when `compiler` or `compiler.version` is not defined.
expectation.conceptual: Recipes should be able to express minimum compiler support with a single standard validator instead of hand-written version checks. When a consumer uses an unsupported compiler version, Conan should reject the configuration with a clear explanation of the required version and why it is required, while missing compiler metadata should fail as an explicit configuration error.

constraints.grounded: `check_min_compiler_version` must be importable from `conan.tools.build`, must only enforce the restriction declared for the active compiler, must not fail when the active compiler has no declared restriction, and must distinguish missing compiler settings from an unsupported compiler version by raising `ConanException` instead of `ConanInvalidConfiguration`.
constraints.conceptual: The new validator should only apply rules that the recipe explicitly declares, should leave unrelated compilers unaffected, and should clearly separate invalid environment metadata from a genuine compiler version incompatibility.

behavior: A new public validator named `check_min_compiler_version` is exposed through `conan.tools.build`.
The validator reads the active compiler name and compiler version from the recipe settings before performing validation.
If either the compiler name or compiler version is unavailable, validation fails immediately with `ConanException`.
If the active compiler matches a declared restriction and its version is lower than the declared minimum, validation fails with `ConanInvalidConfiguration`.
The invalid-configuration failure communicates the recipe identity, the required minimum compiler version, the detected compiler version, and the reason attached to the restriction.
If the active compiler meets or exceeds the declared minimum version, validation succeeds.
If the active compiler is not listed in the declared restrictions, validation succeeds without error.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe imports `check_min_compiler_version` from `conan.tools.build` and calls it during validation with a minimum version for the active compiler, it should allow configurations whose compiler version is equal to or greater than the declared minimum.

When the active compiler version is below the declared minimum for that compiler, the recipe validation should fail with `ConanInvalidConfiguration` and surface both the minimum required version and the reason for the restriction.
When the active compiler is not included in the declared compiler restrictions, the validator should not reject the configuration.
When `settings.compiler` is missing, calling the validator should fail with `ConanException` rather than silently passing or reporting an unsupported version.
When `settings.compiler.version` is missing, calling the validator should fail with `ConanException` rather than silently passing or reporting an unsupported version.

task_3.title: Add support for newer Apple OS and SDK versions
task_3.description: Update the built-in Apple settings model so users can target newer iOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS, and macOS releases in Conan profiles and settings, while keeping unsupported SDK versions out of the accepted value set.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan recognizes the latest released Apple operating system versions and matching SDK versions across iOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS, and macOS, and that unsupported SDK versions remain invalid.

expectation.grounded: The built-in Apple settings validation for `os.version` and `os.sdk_version` must accept these additional values: `iOS` versions `18.5` and `18.6` with SDK version `18.5`; `watchOS` versions `11.5` and `11.6` with SDK version `11.5`; `tvOS` versions `18.5` and `18.6` with SDK version `18.5`; `visionOS` versions `2.5` and `2.6` with SDK version `2.5`; and `Macos` versions `15.5` and `15.6` with SDK version `15.5`. Unsupported SDK values that are not part of the released Apple SDK set, including `18.6` for iOS and tvOS SDKs, must remain rejected.
expectation.conceptual: Users targeting current Apple platform releases should be able to declare those OS and SDK versions in normal Conan settings without validation errors. The accepted SDK list should only include versions Apple has actually released, so speculative or nonexistent SDK versions are not treated as valid.

constraints.grounded: Keep existing Apple setting names and SDK identifiers unchanged, preserve previously supported versions, and extend only the allowed version enumerations for `os.version` and `os.sdk_version`. Do not loosen validation so that unlisted SDK versions are accepted.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should be backward compatible for existing Apple targets while tightening correctness around what SDK versions are considered real and supported.

behavior: `os=iOS` now accepts `os.version=18.5` and `os.version=18.6`.
`os=iOS` now accepts `os.sdk_version=18.5`, but `os.sdk_version=18.6` remains unsupported.
`os=watchOS` now accepts `os.version=11.5` and `os.version=11.6`, and `os.sdk_version=11.5`.
`os=tvOS` now accepts `os.version=18.5` and `os.version=18.6`, and `os.sdk_version=18.5`, while `os.sdk_version=18.6` remains unsupported.
`os=visionOS` now accepts `os.version=2.5` and `os.version=2.6`, and `os.sdk_version=2.5`.
`os=Macos` now accepts `os.version=15.5` and `os.version=15.6`, and `os.sdk_version=15.5`.
acceptance_criteria: When a user sets an iOS target with `os.version` `18.5` or `18.6`, Conan should accept the OS version as valid.
When a user sets an iOS or tvOS target with `os.sdk_version=18.5`, Conan should accept the SDK version as valid.
When a user sets an iOS or tvOS target with `os.sdk_version=18.6`, Conan should reject it as an unsupported SDK version.
When a user sets a watchOS target with `os.version` `11.5` or `11.6` and `os.sdk_version=11.5`, Conan should accept those settings.
When a user sets a visionOS target with `os.version` `2.5` or `2.6` and `os.sdk_version=2.5`, Conan should accept those settings.
When a user sets a macOS target with `os.version` `15.5` or `15.6` and `os.sdk_version=15.5`, Conan should accept those settings.
When users continue using previously valid Apple OS and SDK values, those settings should remain accepted.

task_4.title: Allow opting out of IntelCC environment script generation
task_4.description: Conan 2.20.0 adds a supported way to skip automatic generation of the Intel compiler environment activation script when users intentionally set `tools.intel:installation_path` to an empty string. This lets teams rely on a pre-activated Intel compiler environment instead of Conan creating `conanintelsetvars`, while preserving normal behavior for configured Intel installations.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can disable Conan's automatic Intel compiler environment setup when using `IntelCC` by explicitly setting `tools.intel:installation_path` to an empty string, for cases where the Intel compiler environment has already been activated outside Conan.

expectation.grounded: `IntelCC.generate()` must treat `tools.intel:installation_path=""` as an explicit opt-out and avoid generating the `conanintelsetvars` activation script. When this opt-out is used, Conan should rely on the caller having already activated the Intel compiler environment before running the build flow.
expectation.conceptual: Users who already initialize the Intel compiler environment themselves should be able to tell Conan not to emit its Intel setup script by leaving the Intel installation path intentionally empty.

constraints.grounded: Only the exact empty-string value for `tools.intel:installation_path` should suppress `conanintelsetvars` generation. Existing `IntelCC` behavior for unset or non-empty installation paths must remain unchanged, including normal platform-specific script generation.
constraints.conceptual: This opt-out should be narrow and explicit: it should affect only intentionally empty Intel installation path configurations and should not change the default behavior for normal Intel compiler setups.

behavior: When `tools.intel:installation_path` is explicitly set to an empty string, `IntelCC` does not create a `conanintelsetvars` environment activation script.
The skip applies before any platform-specific Intel setup script content is produced, so no Conan-managed Intel activation script is emitted for that configuration.
Using the empty-string configuration means the Intel compiler environment is expected to be active already outside Conan.
If `tools.intel:installation_path` is unset or contains a non-empty path, `IntelCC` continues generating the Intel environment setup script as before.
acceptance_criteria: Given an `IntelCC` configuration with `tools.intel:installation_path` set to an empty string, when Conan generates the build environment, it should not produce a `conanintelsetvars` activation script.

Given an externally activated Intel compiler environment, when Conan runs with `tools.intel:installation_path` set to an empty string, it should proceed without requiring Conan to generate an Intel environment setup script.
When `tools.intel:installation_path` is not an empty string, Conan should preserve the prior IntelCC behavior and continue generating the Intel activation script appropriate for the environment.

task_5.title: Make generated Conan workspace super-builds follow package names and build order
task_5.description: The 2.20.0 update improves the `conan new workspace` super-build template so the generated top-level CMake project is driven by the workspace's actual build order and package names instead of a fixed sample layout. This allows workspaces to configure correctly when package folders are renamed or differ from package names, while preserving expected namespaced targets for library packages.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that workspaces generated by `conan new workspace` can be used as super-builds even when a package's folder name differs from its Conan package name, and ensure the generated super-build adds projects from the workspace's real build order instead of a hard-coded sample sequence.

expectation.grounded: The `conan new workspace` template should generate a super-build `CMakeLists.txt` that consumes the ordering emitted by `Workspace.build_order`, adds each project using both the Conan package name and its workspace folder, declares `FetchContent` entries by package name with `OVERRIDE_FIND_PACKAGE`, and creates `<package>::<package>` alias targets only for non-executable targets. Running `workspace super-install` should provide the ordering data needed for subsequent CMake preset configuration.
expectation.conceptual: A newly generated Conan workspace should automatically adapt to the packages and dependency order present in that workspace. CMake configuration should continue to work if a package lives in a differently named directory, library packages should still expose the expected namespaced targets, and executable packages should be added without being treated as libraries.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing super-build behavior for the default sample workspace while removing reliance on fixed project names. Keep source resolution tied to each workspace folder, keep package identity tied to the Conan package name for `FetchContent` and namespaced target exposure, and do not create library alias targets for executables.
constraints.conceptual: Existing generated workspaces should keep building in dependency order, but the generated build should no longer depend on folder names matching package names. The update must not misclassify executables as libraries or break the default generated workspace layout.

behavior: The generated super-build no longer hard-codes the sample projects and instead iterates over the workspace build order produced during workspace installation.
Each workspace entry is handled as a package-name and folder-path pair, so source lookup follows the folder while package registration and discovery follow the Conan package name.
CMake configuration output identifies both the package being added and the folder it is loaded from.
After adding a non-executable package, the generated super-build exposes a `<package>::<package>` alias target for consumers.
Executable workspace packages are added to the super-build without creating a library alias target for them.
acceptance_criteria: When a workspace created with `conan new workspace` contains a package whose directory name differs from its Conan package name, running `workspace super-install` and then configuring CMake with the generated preset should succeed.
When the generated super-build processes library packages, consumers should be able to resolve the expected `<package>::<package>` alias targets.
When the generated super-build processes an executable package, it should still be added to the build without exposing it as a library alias target.

When workspace contents or dependency order differ from the original sample layout, the generated super-build should add projects according to the emitted workspace build order rather than a fixed sequence.

task_6.title: Prefer config-based package discovery in CMakeConfigDeps
task_6.description: The update changes CMakeConfigDeps-generated dependency setup so CMake prefers config-package discovery during find_package resolution. This makes Conan-provided package configuration files take precedence when both config-mode and module-mode discovery are possible, while preserving the generator's existing dependency path and directory hints.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that projects using the CMakeConfigDeps generator automatically prefer config-based package discovery so dependency resolution selects generated package configuration files ahead of module-based lookup when both are available.

expectation.grounded: When CMakeConfigDeps generates its CMake dependency setup, it should enable CMAKE_FIND_PACKAGE_PREFER_CONFIG for consumers of that generated configuration. After the generated setup is loaded, downstream find_package() resolution should prefer config packages associated with the generated dependency metadata rather than falling back first to module-mode discovery.
expectation.conceptual: Consumers using the generator should get config-first package discovery by default. If the same dependency could be found either through a package config file or through a Find-module, the config-based result should win without requiring extra user configuration.

constraints.grounded: The change should remain scoped to CMakeConfigDeps-generated dependency configuration, and existing dependency path exports and package directory hints emitted by the generator should continue to be available. The upgrade should not require consumers to manually opt in to config-first behavior when using the generator.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should strengthen dependency resolution precedence without removing existing discovery hints or introducing extra setup steps for users already relying on the generator.

behavior: CMakeConfigDeps-generated dependency setup now turns on CMAKE_FIND_PACKAGE_PREFER_CONFIG for consuming CMake projects.
After the generated dependency setup is loaded, subsequent find_package() calls prefer config-mode package discovery over module-mode discovery.
The config-first preference is applied alongside the generator's existing dependency path and package directory exposure rather than replacing them.
acceptance_criteria: When a project consumes dependencies through CMakeConfigDeps, loading the generated dependency configuration should cause CMake to prefer config-package discovery for later find_package() calls.
When both a package config file and a Find-module are available for the same dependency, dependency resolution should select the config-based package result while using the generated setup.

When upgrading to this version, projects that already rely on the generator's dependency paths and package directory hints should continue to receive those hints in addition to the new config-first preference.

task_7.title: Support exclusion patterns in archive get/unzip APIs
task_7.description: Version 2.20.0 adds a user-facing exclusion filter for archive extraction so callers can omit matching files or directories when using the high-level `get()` helper or the lower-level `unzip()` API. The change is additive and is intended to let consumers unpack only the archive content they want without changing existing behavior for callers that do not request exclusions.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that archive download and extraction workflows can omit unwanted files or directories by pattern when using the public `get()` and `unzip()` APIs, while preserving current behavior for calls that do not request exclusions.

expectation.grounded: `conan.tools.files.get()` and `conan.tools.files.unzip()` should accept an optional `excludes` argument containing Unix shell-style wildcard patterns for archive member paths. During ZIP and TAR-family extraction, any member whose path matches an exclude pattern should be skipped and not extracted. If both `pattern` and `excludes` are supplied, the extraction result should be limited to entries allowed by `pattern` and then filtered to remove entries matching `excludes`. `get()` should forward the exclusion setting to the extraction stage.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to download or unpack archives and specify path patterns that must be left out of the extracted result. Exclusions should work consistently across supported archive formats, combine predictably with existing include filtering, and leave existing callers unaffected unless they opt in.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the observable behavior of `get()` or `unzip()` when `excludes` is not provided. The exclusion option should only affect archive member selection during extraction; existing options such as `pattern` and `strip_root`, as well as normal handling of supported archive types, must continue to operate on the remaining members. Single-file gzip decompression should continue to behave as before.
constraints.conceptual: This should be an additive capability rather than a breaking change. Existing extraction flows should keep working the same way by default, and other extraction options should remain compatible with the filtered result.

behavior: `conan.tools.files.get()` accepts an `excludes` option and applies it when the downloaded archive is unpacked.
`conan.tools.files.unzip()` accepts exclusion patterns and skips ZIP archive entries whose archive paths match any supplied pattern.
`conan.tools.files.unzip()` applies the same exclusion filtering to TAR-based formats it supports, including `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, `.tar.bz2`, `.tbz2`, `.tar.xz`, and `.txz`.
When both include filtering (`pattern`) and exclusion filtering (`excludes`) are used, exclusions still remove matching members from the final extraction set.
When `strip_root` is used together with exclusions, only non-excluded members participate in the extracted output.
If no exclusions are provided, extraction behavior remains unchanged from the previous version.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller uses `unzip()` with an archive containing multiple paths and provides one or more `excludes` patterns, it should extract only members whose archive paths do not match those patterns.
When a caller uses `get()` with `excludes`, the downloaded archive should be unpacked with the same exclusion behavior as calling `unzip()` directly.
When both `pattern` and `excludes` are provided, a member that matches the include pattern but also matches an exclude pattern should not appear in the extracted output.
When `strip_root` is enabled together with `excludes`, excluded members should remain omitted and retained members should still be extracted with root stripping applied.
When `excludes` is omitted, archive extraction should behave the same as it did before this update.

task_8.title: Add GCC 15.2 compiler support
task_8.description: Conan 2.20.0 adds support for GCC 15.2 by recognizing it as a valid compiler version in user settings. This allows profiles and build configurations targeting GCC 15.2 to be accepted the same way as other supported GCC releases.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan accepts GCC 15.2 as a supported `compiler.version` for `compiler=gcc`, so users can configure profiles and builds for that toolchain without unsupported-setting failures.

expectation.grounded: When `compiler=gcc`, the accepted `compiler.version` values must include `15.2`. Any Conan operation that validates user-provided settings, including profiles and explicit setting overrides, should accept `compiler.version=15.2` and continue normal processing instead of rejecting that configuration as an invalid GCC version.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to target GCC 15.2 anywhere they declare Conan compiler settings, and the tool should treat that compiler release as officially supported rather than unknown or invalid.

constraints.grounded: The change is additive: GCC `15.2` becomes an accepted value for `compiler.version` when `compiler=gcc`, while previously supported GCC versions remain accepted and unrelated compiler settings keep their existing behavior. No alternate version remapping, new warnings, or broader compiler-policy changes are implied.
constraints.conceptual: Support for the new compiler release should not disturb existing working configurations. The upgrade should only expand the set of valid GCC versions and leave other compiler behavior unchanged.

behavior: `compiler=gcc` now recognizes `compiler.version=15.2` as a valid supported setting value.
Profiles or other user-supplied Conan settings that specify GCC 15.2 should pass settings validation instead of failing because the compiler version is unsupported.
Once accepted, GCC 15.2 configurations should proceed through Conan's normal dependency and build configuration flow used for other supported GCC versions.
Previously supported GCC versions, including earlier 15.x values, remain valid with unchanged behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a user defines `compiler=gcc` and `compiler.version=15.2` in a Conan profile, the profile should be accepted as valid.
When a user supplies `compiler=gcc` and `compiler.version=15.2` through Conan settings overrides, the command should not fail due to GCC 15.2 being an unsupported compiler version.
When GCC 15.2 is selected, Conan should handle the configuration the same way it handles other supported GCC versions, without special fallback behavior.
When users continue to use GCC versions that were already supported before this upgrade, those configurations should keep working unchanged.

task_9.title: Add newer Apple platform versions to Conan default settings
task_9.description: Conan 2.20.0 expands the built-in Apple settings template so newer Apple OS and SDK versions are recognized out of the box. This primarily delivers iOS 18.5 and tvOS 18.5 support from the release note, while the shipped settings data also adds corresponding newer values for watchOS, visionOS, and macOS, reducing the need for users to maintain custom settings entries.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan's default Apple settings recognize newly released Apple platform versions so users can target current iOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS, and macOS releases without custom settings edits or invalid setting rejections.

expectation.grounded: The default Conan settings template must extend the allowed `os.version` and `os.sdk_version` values for Apple platforms. `iOS` must accept `18.5` and `18.6` as `os.version`, and `18.5` as `os.sdk_version`. `tvOS` must accept `18.5` and `18.6` as `os.version`, and `18.5` as `os.sdk_version`. `watchOS` must accept `11.5` and `11.6` as `os.version`, and `11.5` as `os.sdk_version`. `visionOS` must accept `2.5` and `2.6` as `os.version`, and `2.5` as `os.sdk_version`. `Macos` must accept `15.5` and `15.6` as `os.version`, and `15.5` as `os.sdk_version`.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to declare current Apple OS and SDK versions in Conan's default settings without being forced to patch the shipped settings list themselves.

constraints.grounded: This update should only expand the accepted Apple version catalogs in the default settings data. Existing Apple `sdk` names, previously supported `os.version` and `os.sdk_version` values, and existing nullable entries must remain valid and unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should add support for newer Apple platform versions without breaking any existing settings combinations that already worked.

behavior: Conan's default settings now include `iOS` `os.version` values `18.5` and `18.6`, and `iOS` `os.sdk_version` value `18.5`.
Conan's default settings now include `tvOS` `os.version` values `18.5` and `18.6`, and `tvOS` `os.sdk_version` value `18.5`.
Conan's default settings now include `watchOS` `os.version` values `11.5` and `11.6`, and `watchOS` `os.sdk_version` value `11.5`.
Conan's default settings now include `visionOS` `os.version` values `2.5` and `2.6`, and `visionOS` `os.sdk_version` value `2.5`.
Conan's default settings now include `Macos` `os.version` values `15.5` and `15.6`, and `Macos` `os.sdk_version` value `15.5`.
Profiles or package settings that use these newly listed Apple values should be treated as valid by the shipped settings catalog instead of requiring user-maintained additions.
acceptance_criteria: When a user targets `iOS` with `os.version` set to `18.5` or `18.6`, Conan should recognize the value as valid in the default settings.
When a user targets `iOS` with `os.sdk_version` set to `18.5`, Conan should recognize the value as valid in the default settings.
When a user targets `tvOS` with `os.version` set to `18.5` or `18.6`, and `os.sdk_version` set to `18.5`, Conan should recognize those values as valid in the default settings.
When a user targets `watchOS` with `os.version` set to `11.5` or `11.6`, and `os.sdk_version` set to `11.5`, Conan should recognize those values as valid in the default settings.
When a user targets `visionOS` with `os.version` set to `2.5` or `2.6`, and `os.sdk_version` set to `2.5`, Conan should recognize those values as valid in the default settings.
When a user targets `Macos` with `os.version` set to `15.5` or `15.6`, and `os.sdk_version` set to `15.5`, Conan should recognize those values as valid in the default settings.
When users continue using previously supported Apple version values, those existing values should remain accepted.

task_11.title: Expose and honor workspace super-install build order
task_11.description: The upgrade makes `conan workspace super-install` surface the dependency-based build order of editable workspace packages and exposes that ordered workspace data so custom workspaces, including generated CMake-based workspaces, can add projects in a dependency-safe sequence instead of relying on a fixed order.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan workspace super-install` reports the dependency-safe build order of editable workspace packages and makes that same ordered workspace information available to workspace definitions so generated builds can add projects consistently and in the correct order.

expectation.grounded: `conan workspace super-install` should derive an ordered list of editable workspace packages from the dependency graph, call `Workspace.build_order(order)` before collapsing the workspace graph, and preserve each package's reference and workspace folder in that callback data. The default `Workspace.build_order()` behavior should emit the ordered package references to command output, and generated workspace integrations should be able to consume the ordered package-name/folder mapping to add workspace projects in that order.
expectation.conceptual: Running the workspace super-install flow should show users which local packages are built first and allow workspace-specific build integrations to follow that exact dependency order when assembling the overall build.

constraints.grounded: The reported order must reflect only editable packages that are part of the workspace and must preserve dependency-level ordering from the original graph. The new ordering support must not change package selection, binary analysis, or profile- and option-driven workspace root configuration during `workspace super-install`, and generated CMake workspaces must avoid treating executable targets as library aliases.
constraints.conceptual: The feature should add build-order visibility and ordered workspace generation without changing which packages are installed or built, and it should keep build-system integration safe for both libraries and executables.

behavior: `conan workspace super-install` now reports editable workspace packages in dependency order before the workspace graph is collapsed.
`Workspace.build_order(order)` is a workspace hook that receives the ordered workspace packages, including enough information to identify each package and its workspace location.
Generated workspace scaffolding can persist the ordered workspace package list and reuse it to add projects to an external build system in the computed order instead of a hard-coded sequence.
When generated CMake workspace logic processes the ordered packages, it creates namespace aliases only for non-executable targets.

The workspace root ConanFile is initialized with the selected profiles and package options before the collapsed workspace graph is created, so option-sensitive workspace behavior remains available during super-install.
acceptance_criteria: When a workspace contains multiple editable packages with dependency relationships and `conan workspace super-install` is run, the command should display those workspace package references in dependency-safe build order.

When a workspace overrides `Workspace.build_order(order)`, it should receive the ordered editable workspace packages before the collapsed workspace graph is generated, and each item should identify both the package and its workspace folder.
When a generated CMake-based workspace consumes the emitted build-order data, it should add workspace projects according to the computed order rather than a fixed package list.
When the ordered workspace packages include executables, the generated CMake-based workspace should add those projects without creating library aliases for them.

When the workspace root configuration depends on selected profiles or package options, `workspace super-install` should still honor that configuration while adding the new build-order reporting behavior.

task_10.title: Stabilize the public Conan ConfigAPI
task_10.description: Conan 2.20.0 formalizes ConfigAPI as the supported Python sub-API for working with Conan home configuration. The public surface is narrowed to documented methods for reading, listing, installing, and cleaning configuration, and configuration installs now refresh ConanAPI state so subsequent operations observe the updated settings immediately.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Python integrations use the stabilized ConfigAPI surface to inspect and manage Conan configuration, and that configuration changes become visible immediately through public API calls without depending on internal configuration objects or loaders.

expectation.grounded: Provide ConfigAPI as the supported Conan Python sub-API for configuration management through the public methods home(), install(...), install_pkg(...), get(name, default=None, check_type=None), show(pattern), conf_list(), and clean(). install() must support configuration sources from git repositories, HTTP zip files, and local directories, and it must reinitialize ConanAPI after applying changes. install_pkg() must install configuration from a Conan package, return the resulting PkgReference, and reinitialize ConanAPI after installation. get() must read from the active global.conf with optional default fallback and type checking, show() must return matching global.conf entries as a mapping, and conf_list() must expose the built-in configuration catalog without exposing the internal registry object. Consumers should not rely on ConfigAPI.global_conf, ConfigAPI.builtin_confs, ConfigAPI.settings_yml, or ConfigAPI.load_config(...) as part of the supported public surface.
expectation.conceptual: Applications embedding Conan should use a small, documented configuration API to discover the active Conan home, install configuration from supported sources, read individual or filtered configuration values, list built-in settings, clean user configuration, and install configuration packages. After any configuration install, later API calls should immediately observe the updated settings through the public methods.

constraints.grounded: clean() must preserve the package storage directory resolved from core.cache:storage_path or the default package storage under the Conan home. home() is for inspecting the active Conan home path and must not be treated as permission to modify or remove cached packages directly. Command-line core configuration overrides must remain reflected in subsequent ConfigAPI.get() reads after ConanAPI reinitialization.
constraints.conceptual: Resetting configuration must not delete cached packages. Callers should rely only on the supported configuration methods rather than internal state objects. Temporary configuration overrides applied to the active API session should remain visible through normal configuration reads once they take effect.

behavior: ConfigAPI.get() reads the current global configuration value, supports default fallbacks, and supports typed retrieval via check_type.
ConfigAPI.show(pattern) returns the set of global configuration entries that match the requested pattern.
ConfigAPI.conf_list() returns the built-in configuration definitions as an independent mapping.
ConfigAPI.install() applies configuration from supported external sources and immediately reinitializes ConanAPI so other sub-APIs use the new configuration.

ConfigAPI.install_pkg() installs configuration from a Conan package, returns the installed PkgReference, and avoids repeating the install when the same configuration package is already active unless forced.
ConfigAPI.clean() resets user configuration in the Conan home while leaving package storage intact.
ConanAPI exposes a read-only home_folder and centralizes configuration reloading so subsequent operations see the current configuration.
acceptance_criteria: When an integration calls conan_api.config.get() for a global.conf key, it should receive the active value or the supplied default, with type enforcement when check_type is provided.
When an integration calls conan_api.config.show(pattern), it should receive a mapping containing only configuration entries matching that pattern.

When an integration calls conan_api.config.conf_list(), it should receive the available built-in configuration keys and descriptions without mutating Conan's internal built-in registry through the returned object.

When configuration is installed through conan_api.config.install(...), later reads through conan_api.config.get() and dependent Conan APIs should reflect the new configuration without requiring a new ConanAPI instance.

When configuration is installed through conan_api.config.install_pkg(...), the call should return the installed PkgReference and the installed configuration should become active immediately after the call completes.
When conan_api.config.clean() is executed, custom configuration state should be reset while the package storage directory remains preserved.

task_12.title: Aggregate options for workspace super-build roots
task_12.description: Conan 2.20.0 improves workspace super-builds so a workspace root ConanFile can observe the effective host options and settings used for the super-build and inspect the resolved option values of editable workspace packages. This enables root-level generation and orchestration logic to stay aligned with workspace package configuration.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that a workspace super-build propagates effective root-level configuration into the workspace root ConanFile and aggregates the resolved options of editable workspace packages so root-level workspace logic can make consistent build and generation decisions.

expectation.grounded: When a `Workspace` defines `root_conanfile()`, `workspace super-install` should initialize that root `ConanFile` with the host profile before root-level generation logic runs, so its `settings` and `options` reflect the effective current-package option values supplied by profiles or CLI options. Standard root recipe option processing should apply in this flow, including `config_options()`, `configure()`, automatic language-related option cleanup, and `implements = "auto_shared_fpic"` behavior when relevant. The root `ConanFile` should also expose `workspace_packages_options`, keyed by editable package reference, containing each workspace package's serialized effective option values. The root package's own `options` object should contain only current-package values, not dependency option namespaces.
expectation.conceptual: Running a workspace super-build should give the workspace's root project a faithful view of the resolved configuration: it should see its own effective options and settings, and it should be able to inspect the final option values of each editable workspace package from a single aggregated structure.

constraints.grounded: Only editable workspace packages should be aggregated into `workspace_packages_options`; non-editable dependencies should remain regular collapsed-graph dependencies. Root-recipe option resolution in super-build mode should preserve normal Conan semantics, including option normalization hooks, while keeping per-dependency option state out of the root package's own `options` object.
constraints.conceptual: The feature should add visibility into workspace package configuration without changing unrelated dependency handling or mixing the root project's own options with per-package option data.

behavior: `workspace super-install` now prepares the `Workspace.root_conanfile()` consumer with host settings and root-level option values before root-level recipe logic observes them.

The root workspace recipe's option lifecycle is applied in super-build mode, so `config_options()`, `configure()`, and compatible automatic `shared`/`fPIC` behavior can change the final options seen by the root recipe.
The root conanfile receives `workspace_packages_options`, keyed by editable package reference, with each workspace package's serialized effective option values.
The root conanfile's own `options` reflect only current-package/root values rather than merged dependency option namespaces.
Only editable workspace packages contribute to the aggregated workspace option mapping; non-editable dependencies continue through the collapsed graph normally.
acceptance_criteria: Given a workspace that defines `root_conanfile()`, when `workspace super-install` is invoked with host options for the root recipe, the root conanfile should observe the effective option values through `self.options` during normal recipe logic such as generation.

Given a root workspace recipe that customizes options through `config_options()` or `configure()`, when `workspace super-install` runs, the observable final option state should honor those hooks in the same super-build execution.

Given a root workspace recipe that relies on Conan's automatic `shared`/`fPIC` behavior, when host settings or `shared` option values make `fPIC` inapplicable, the root recipe should observe the normalized final option state rather than an unfiltered raw input.

Given editable workspace packages with resolved options, when the workspace graph is collapsed for a super-build, the root conanfile should be able to inspect each editable package's effective option values through `workspace_packages_options`, keyed by package reference.
Given external non-editable dependencies in the graph, when the root conanfile inspects `workspace_packages_options`, those external dependencies should not appear in that aggregated mapping.

task_13.title: Support install_strip in Autotools installs
task_13.description: Conan 2.20.0 extends the existing tools.build:install_strip configuration to Autotools so default Autotools package installs can strip installed binaries, aligning Autotools with the behavior already available for CMake and Meson.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Autotools-based package installs honor the tools.build:install_strip configuration so users can request stripped install artifacts through the standard Conan build configuration.

expectation.grounded: When using conan.tools.gnu.Autotools, calling Autotools.install() without an explicit target must consult the boolean tools.build:install_strip configuration. If the configuration is enabled, the helper must invoke the install-strip target; otherwise it must invoke the normal install target. If a target is explicitly supplied to Autotools.install(), that target must remain in effect instead of being replaced by install-strip.
expectation.conceptual: Autotools installs should support the same strip-on-install option already available in other Conan build helpers. Enabling the strip configuration should make the default install step produce stripped installed binaries, while explicit custom install targets should continue to behave exactly as requested by the caller.

constraints.grounded: The change is limited to default target resolution in Autotools.install(). Existing args, makefile selection, and DESTDIR install behavior must remain intact, and disabling or omitting tools.build:install_strip must preserve the normal install target.
constraints.conceptual: Only the default install behavior should change when strip-on-install is requested. Existing install customization and non-strip installs must keep working without behavior changes.

behavior: The built-in Conan configuration tools.build:install_strip now applies to Autotools in addition to CMake and Meson.
Autotools.install() now resolves its default target dynamically: install when strip-on-install is disabled or absent, and install-strip when strip-on-install is enabled.
Passing an explicit target to Autotools.install() bypasses the automatic install versus install-strip selection.
The observable runtime effect of enabling the configuration is that the Autotools install step uses the strip-aware install target during package installation.
acceptance_criteria: When tools.build:install_strip is unset or false and Autotools.install() is called without a target, it should execute the standard install target.
When tools.build:install_strip is true and Autotools.install() is called without a target, it should execute the install-strip target.
When Autotools.install() is called with an explicit target, it should honor that target regardless of the tools.build:install_strip setting.
When install arguments or a custom makefile are provided, they should continue to be applied alongside the resolved target without changing existing install customization behavior.

task_15.title: Clarify build-folder file conflict failures
task_15.description: The upgrade improves how Conan reports build setup failures when the configured build folder path is already occupied by a regular file. Instead of falling through to a generic directory-creation failure, the build now stops with a clearer, path-specific error so users can immediately identify and fix the file-versus-directory conflict.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan build` detects when the configured build folder location is already occupied by a file and fails with a clear, user-facing explanation of the conflict.

expectation.grounded: When `conan build` initializes `ConanFile.build_folder`, it should check whether that path already exists as a regular file. If so, it should stop build-folder setup and raise `ConanException` that clearly indicates the build folder could not be created because a file already exists at that path. If no such file conflict exists, normal creation of the build folder and package metadata folder should proceed unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: Starting a build should immediately surface an actionable error if the chosen build directory name collides with an existing file. Users should be told that the build directory cannot be created at that location and which path caused the problem, while unaffected builds continue to work normally.

constraints.grounded: Do not change successful build flows when the resolved build folder path is absent or already usable as a directory. Limit the new failure handling to the case where the build folder path exists as a file, and preserve the existing build initialization sequence otherwise.
constraints.conceptual: Only the invalid file-conflict case should change. Normal builds and valid directory-based layouts should behave the same as before.

behavior: Before creating the build folder, Conan checks whether the resolved build folder path is an existing regular file.
If a file is found at the intended build folder path, the build aborts immediately with `ConanException` rather than continuing into generic directory creation.
The failure clearly identifies that the conflict is between the expected build directory and an already existing file at the same path.
When there is no file conflict at the build folder path, build-folder creation and package metadata folder creation continue with the existing behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When `conan build` runs for a recipe whose configured build folder path resolves to an existing file, it should fail before entering the build directory and surface a `ConanException` describing the file-versus-directory conflict for that path.

When `conan build` runs and the configured build folder path does not already exist as a file, it should continue creating the build folder and associated metadata folders as part of normal build initialization.

When users encounter this conflict, the reported error should make it clear that the failure is caused by an existing file occupying the build folder location, so the corrective action is understandable without inspecting internal implementation details.

task_14.title: Version-aware system package installs and stricter APT package detection
task_14.description: The system package manager helpers now support requesting specific package versions through the normalized package specifier format, and APT package detection is tightened so packages are only treated as installed when the architecture and, when requested, version actually match.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the system package tool accepts version-qualified package requests and only reports APT packages as already installed when the installed package matches the requested architecture and, when specified, the requested version.

expectation.grounded: The system package manager helpers in `conan.tools.system.package_manager` should accept package entries in the normalized `name=version` form and translate them to each backend's public install syntax where supported, including `Apt`, `Yum`, `Dnf`, `Brew`, `Pkg`, `PkgUtil`, `Chocolatey`, `Apk`, and `Zypper`. `check()` and install-time missing-package detection should evaluate the original package specifier so exact-version checks can be performed when a backend supports them. For `Apt`, installed detection should only succeed when the installed package architecture matches the requested architecture or is architecture-independent (`all`), and if a version is specified it should also require that exact installed version. If a version is requested for a backend that cannot validate exact versions, the tool should warn and continue without claiming exact-version enforcement.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to request a specific system package version through the system package tool and have supported package managers install and detect that exact version. APT should stop treating a package as present just because the same package name exists under a different architecture. When an exact version cannot be verified by the underlying package manager, the tool should remain usable while making that limitation visible.

constraints.grounded: Unversioned package requests must continue to behave as before. Cross-building architecture qualification must remain limited to host packages when that package manager supports architecture-qualified package names; build-machine packages and archless configurations must remain unqualified. APT must continue to recognize architecture-independent `all` packages as satisfying the request.
constraints.conceptual: Existing recipes that request plain package names should not regress. Cross-build behavior should continue distinguishing host packages from build-machine tools, and architecture-independent packages should still count as valid while false positives across architectures are eliminated.

behavior: The system package tool now accepts package specifiers in `name=version` form and maps them to backend-specific versioned package arguments for supported package managers.

Version-qualified package requests preserve existing host-versus-build architecture handling, so host packages remain architecture-qualified during cross-building where supported and build-machine packages do not.
Installed-package detection now evaluates the original package specifier, enabling exact-version checks on package managers that expose version-aware queries.
APT installed detection now validates package architecture and only reports success when the installed package matches the requested architecture or is `all`.
When a version is requested on APT, the installed package must also match that exact version to be treated as present.
If the selected package manager cannot guarantee exact version verification, the tool should fall back to non-version-specific detection with a warning instead of failing outright.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan recipe requests a system package as `name=version` through the system package tool on a backend with versioned package syntax, it should attempt installation using that backend's native versioned package format.

When a version-qualified package request is checked on APT, it should only be considered installed if the package exists for the requested architecture or as `all`, and the installed version matches the requested version.
When the same package name is installed on APT only for a different architecture, the system package tool should treat the requested package as missing rather than already installed.

When cross-building a host package with a version-qualified request, the package identifier should continue targeting the host architecture where the backend supports architecture-qualified packages; when requesting a build-machine package, no host-architecture qualifier should be added.
When a version-qualified request is used with a backend that cannot verify exact versions, the tool should continue operating and surface that exact-version validation is not guaranteed.
When a package is requested without a version, installation and detection behavior should remain consistent with prior releases.

task_16.title: Normalize multi-arch names in cmake_layout build folders
task_16.description: The upgrade fixes `cmake_layout` so Apple universal or multi-architecture `arch` values are normalized when they are incorporated into generated build folder names. This prevents layout-derived paths and related generated names from using the raw multi-arch separator and makes multi-arch builds behave consistently.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `cmake_layout` correctly handles Apple universal or multi-architecture `arch` setting values when those values are used to derive folder names, so multi-arch builds produce usable and consistent layout output.

expectation.grounded: When `cmake_layout` derives build folder custom variables from `settings.arch`, it should treat Apple multi-arch or universal values as a special case and normalize the architecture separator before using the value in generated folder names or other layout-derived names. Single-architecture values should continue to be used as before.
expectation.conceptual: Projects using `cmake_layout` should be able to use Apple multi-architecture build settings without getting malformed or inconsistent generated folder names. The layout should expose a stable, filesystem-friendly name for multi-arch builds while preserving existing behavior for normal architecture values.

constraints.grounded: The normalization should apply to the public `cmake_layout` behavior only when the derived custom variable comes from `settings.arch` and contains the Apple multi-arch separator. Other settings and option-derived folder variables should remain unaffected, and non-multi-arch `arch` values should not change.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be narrowly scoped to multi-architecture folder naming and must not alter unrelated layout variables or ordinary single-architecture builds.

behavior: `cmake_layout` now normalizes `settings.arch` values that represent Apple multi-architecture builds before using them in generated folder names.
Multi-arch architecture values no longer propagate the raw Apple universal separator into layout-derived directory naming.
Single-architecture `arch` values and non-`arch` folder variables retain their previous behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a project uses `cmake_layout` and the selected `arch` value represents an Apple multi-architecture build, the generated build folder name should use a normalized architecture token instead of the raw multi-arch separator.
When a project uses `cmake_layout` with a normal single-architecture `arch` value, the generated folder naming should remain unchanged.
When build folder naming includes other settings or options, those values should continue to be handled the same way as before.

task_17.title: Clarify and harden ConanOutput text message handling
task_17.description: Conan 2.20.0 makes the public ConanOutput messaging interface clearer and avoids a newline-handling failure when some non-string values reach output methods. The API is still defined around text messages, not arbitrary object logging.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that ConanOutput public messaging methods remain text-oriented APIs, are clearly documented for their intended verbosity/notice usage, and do not fail during output solely because an emitted message value is not already a string when newline-terminated output is produced.

expectation.grounded: ConanOutput.trace(), debug(), verbose(), status()/info(), title(), subtitle(), highlight(), and success() should present a documented public contract that their message argument is text. ConanOutput.info should continue to behave as an alias of status. If one of these methods emits output with a trailing newline, the write path should not raise a type-concatenation failure only because the supplied message value is not already a Python str; however, this must not be treated as support for passing arbitrary objects to .info() and similar methods.
expectation.conceptual: The output API should be easier to understand and more tolerant of accidental non-string message values during normal text emission, while still making it clear that callers are expected to provide text messages rather than rely on generic object-to-string behavior.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the existing public method names or the info-to-status alias, do not alter the current verbosity/notice gating associated with these methods, and do not expand the supported contract from text messages to arbitrary object payloads.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the logging surface and visibility rules stable, preserve backwards-compatible method semantics, and avoid implying that any object type is a supported message input.

behavior: The ConanOutput public messaging methods are explicitly documented as text-based interfaces, including their intended severity or verbosity usage.
ConanOutput.info continues to map to the status-level output behavior.
When a message is emitted with a trailing newline, the final value written to the stream is handled as text instead of relying on direct string concatenation with the original object.
The update reduces avoidable failures from incidental non-string inputs during output emission, but it does not make arbitrary objects a supported input contract for .info() and similar methods.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller uses ConanOutput.info() or another public ConanOutput messaging method with a value that has a text representation and the message is emitted, the call should not fail solely because newline handling attempted to concatenate a non-string object with a string.
When a caller reads or inspects the ConanOutput public messaging API, the methods should clearly indicate that their message input is text and what kind of output each method represents.
When existing integrations call ConanOutput.info(), it should continue to behave like status() rather than introducing a new output category.
When callers pass arbitrary non-text objects to .info() and similar methods, the library should not treat that usage as a newly supported contract.

task_19.title: Drop Python 3.6 support and require Python 3.7+
task_19.description: Conan 2.20.0 removes Python 3.6 support. Users must upgrade their runtime to Python 3.7 or newer to install and run this release, and unsupported interpreters now fail immediately instead of being only warned about.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to Conan 2.20.0 is treated as a Python runtime compatibility change: Conan must only support Python 3.7 and newer, and users on Python 3.6 must be prevented from installing or running it.

expectation.grounded: Conan 2.20.0 should advertise and enforce a minimum supported interpreter of Python 3.7. Creating `ConanAPI` on Python 3.6 or older Python 3 versions should raise `ConanException` instead of continuing. Python 2 should remain unsupported. The CLI should no longer emit a Python 3.6 deprecation warning because Python 3.6 is no longer a supported runtime.
expectation.conceptual: The upgraded release must require Python 3.7 or newer everywhere users install or run Conan. Unsupported interpreters should be rejected immediately rather than allowed to continue with a warning.

constraints.grounded: Support for Python 3.7 and newer should remain intact for normal CLI and API startup. The change should be limited to compatibility enforcement and supported-version signaling, without changing Conan feature behavior on supported Python versions.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should only tighten the minimum Python version boundary. Users already on supported Python versions should keep the same Conan behavior apart from updated compatibility rules.

behavior: Package installation metadata declares Python 3.7 as the minimum supported interpreter, so Python 3.6 environments are no longer eligible to install the release.
Runtime initialization through `ConanAPI` fails fast with `ConanException` on Python 3.6 or older Python 3 versions instead of starting successfully.
The CLI no longer shows a Python 3.6 deprecation warning because Python 3.6 is treated as unsupported rather than deprecated.
Published supported Python version metadata is updated to list maintained Python 3 releases and omit Python 3.6.
acceptance_criteria: When a user attempts to install Conan 2.20.0 in a Python 3.6 environment, the release should be rejected as requiring Python 3.7 or newer.
When an integration creates `ConanAPI` under Python 3.6, it should raise `ConanException` and not complete initialization.
When the Conan CLI is started under Python 3.7 or newer, it should run without any Python 3.6 deprecation warning.
When users run Conan on supported Python versions, the upgrade should not introduce new runtime compatibility warnings related to the removed Python 3.6 support.

task_18.title: Stabilize and document the ConanOutput text logging API
task_18.description: Conan 2.20.0 clarifies ConanOutput as a documented public logging interface for recipes and custom tools, aligns its message helpers around a text-oriented contract, and removes a small class of output failures caused by newline handling without changing existing verbosity or warning escalation behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `ConanOutput` exposes a clearly documented public logging interface and that its message methods behave consistently as text-oriented, chainable APIs without incidental output failures during newline handling.

expectation.grounded: `ConanOutput(scope="")` should be treated as a documented public interface, accessed through recipe `self.output` or instantiated directly in custom commands and tools. Its public message methods (`trace`, `debug`, `verbose`, `status`/`info`, `title`, `subtitle`, `highlight`, `success`, `warning`, `error`, and `box`) should remain text-oriented APIs, return the current `ConanOutput` instance for chaining, and avoid failing solely because newline handling appends to a non-string intermediate value. Existing warning escalation behavior driven by `warn_tag` matching and warnings-as-errors settings should remain unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: Upgrading users should get a clearly documented `ConanOutput` API with consistent chaining behavior across its logging methods. The logging surface remains intended for text messages, but the upgrade should eliminate incidental type errors caused by newline processing rather than broaden the API into general object serialization.

constraints.grounded: `info` must continue to behave as the `status` alias, existing verbosity filtering must be preserved, optional `scope` prefixing must keep its current meaning, and `warning(..., warn_tag=...)` / `error(..., error_type=...)` semantics must not regress. The change must not redefine these output methods as supporting arbitrary non-text payloads.
constraints.conceptual: Keep current log levels, scoping, filtering, and warning-to-error behavior intact. Improve robustness and documentation of the output API without changing it into a generic formatter for arbitrary objects.

behavior: `ConanOutput` is explicitly presented as a public output class for recipe authors and custom Conan tooling.
`ConanOutput.__init__` continues to accept an optional `scope` string that prefixes emitted messages.
The public logging methods are defined as text-oriented APIs that return the same `ConanOutput` instance for fluent chaining, and `box()` now follows that chaining contract as well.
When output writing needs to add a trailing newline, it should not fail merely because the value being written is not already a plain string.
Warning and error output must continue to honor existing warnings-as-errors escalation behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe uses `self.output` or a custom tool instantiates `ConanOutput`, the available public constructor and message methods should be documented as supported usage.
When any public output method is called with text, it should return the same `ConanOutput` object so calls can be chained.
When `box()` is used before or after another output call in a chain, it should not break fluent usage.
When newline output is requested during message writing, Conan should not raise an error solely because a newline is being appended to a non-string intermediate value.
When callers pass arbitrary non-text objects to `info()` or similar methods, the API contract should still be understood as text-only rather than guaranteed object-to-string conversion support.
When warnings-as-errors is enabled, warning and error handling should behave the same as before the upgrade.

task_22.title: Suppress conflicting visibility risk warnings for test_requires
task_22.description: Version 2.20.0 narrows Conan's conflicting-visibility risk warning so test-only dependency edges introduced with test_requires no longer trigger that warning. Visibility mismatches in the non-test dependency graph should still be reported as before.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that conflicting dependency visibility is not reported as a risk when the conflict comes from test_requires, while preserving the existing warning for equivalent conflicts in normal non-test requirements.

expectation.grounded: When Conan resolves the dependency graph and encounters the same package with different visible settings, it should continue to report the conflicting-visibility risk only for non-test requirement combinations. If either side of that visibility mismatch is introduced through test_requires, the graph should aggregate the requirement without emitting that risk warning.
expectation.conceptual: Test-only dependency paths should not be treated as risky public visibility conflicts. Users should only see the conflicting-visibility warning when the mismatch affects the regular dependency graph rather than test-specific requirements.

constraints.grounded: Do not change how real graph conflicts are handled, and do not suppress the existing conflicting-visibility warning for non-test requirements. The relaxation applies only to the warning generated by mixed visible values when one of the participating requirements is a test_requires edge.
constraints.conceptual: Keep dependency resolution behavior stable except for removing this specific warning noise from test-only scenarios. Ordinary visibility conflicts outside test requirements must continue to surface.

behavior: A visible versus non-visible mismatch for the same dependency no longer produces the conflicting-visibility risk warning when at least one occurrence comes from test_requires.
The existing conflicting-visibility risk warning remains in place for mismatches that arise only from non-test requirements.
This change relaxes warning emission only; it does not redefine unrelated dependency conflict handling.
acceptance_criteria: When the same dependency is reached with opposite visible settings and one path is introduced via test_requires, dependency graph resolution should complete without emitting the conflicting-visibility risk warning for that case.
When the same dependency is reached with opposite visible settings through non-test requirements, Conan should still emit the conflicting-visibility risk warning.
When other kinds of dependency conflicts occur, they should continue to behave as before and should not be masked by this warning relaxation.

task_21.title: Migrate Conan API consumers to ListAPI.select and immutable home folder
task_21.description: Conan 2.20.0 removes the public SearchAPI, consolidates recipe and package querying under ListAPI.select(), makes ConanAPI.home_folder read-only, and requires Python 3.7 or newer. Upgrading integrations must move to the supported list-based query flow and stop relying on post-construction home-folder mutation.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to Conan 2.20.0 preserves recipe and package discovery through the supported public API, prevents workflows from mutating ConanAPI.home_folder after initialization, and only runs on supported Python runtimes.

expectation.grounded: ConanAPI.search and SearchAPI.recipes() are no longer part of the supported public API. Consumers must obtain recipe and package matches through ConanAPI.list.select(pattern: ListPattern, package_query=None, remote=None, lru=None, profile=None), which returns a PackagesList. ListAPI.select() must continue to search either the local cache or a specified Remote, preserve wildcard recipe matching, honor ListPattern-based version filtering, keep the special query suffix '@' behavior that restricts matches to references without user/channel, and raise ConanException when package_query is combined with a non-pattern package_id. ConanAPI.home_folder must be exposed as read-only state, so callers cannot relocate the home/cache by mutating the attribute after construction. ConanAPI initialization must reject Python versions below 3.7, and cache_folder must still be an absolute path.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, recipe and package lookup should still be available, but only through the consolidated listing API. Users should be able to query local or remote data, apply supported filters, and receive deterministic results without relying on a separate search namespace. The configured Conan home location should be fixed at construction time rather than mutable later, and the library should only run on supported Python versions.

constraints.grounded: Do not reintroduce SearchAPI or require consumers to call undocumented/private ListAPI helpers. Preserve the observable query semantics of ListAPI.select(), including local-versus-remote lookup, ListPattern filtering, lru/profile/package_query filtering, deterministic recipe ordering, and the '@' suffix behavior for references with no user/channel. Keep ConanAPI.home_folder non-mutable and preserve validation that cache_folder is absolute.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must narrow the public API surface without changing the meaning of supported search and listing operations. Existing integrations should only need to move to the supported entry point and runtime, while keeping the same visible lookup behavior and without regaining the ability to silently repoint the Conan home directory during execution.

behavior: The public ConanAPI.search entry point and the SearchAPI.recipes() API are removed.
ConanAPI.list.select() becomes the supported public API for recipe and package selection and returns a PackagesList for a provided ListPattern.
ListAPI.select() searches a specified remote when remote is provided and otherwise searches the local cache.
Recipe queries ending with '@' only include references whose user and channel are unset.
ListAPI.select() rejects package_query when the requested package_id is exact rather than a pattern by raising ConanException.

ConanAPI.home_folder is read-only after construction, so changing the effective home/cache location requires creating ConanAPI with the desired constructor value instead of mutating the attribute later.
ConanAPI now requires Python 3.7 or newer at initialization time.
acceptance_criteria: When an integration upgrades to Conan 2.20.0, recipe and package discovery should be performed successfully through ConanAPI.list.select(...) using a ListPattern.
When ListAPI.select(...) is called with a remote, it should query that remote; when no remote is provided, it should query the local cache.
When a recipe query uses wildcard matching or version-constrained selection, the returned matches should remain filtered according to the ListPattern and be deterministically ordered.
When a recipe query ends with '@', the results should only contain references with no user/channel.
When package_query is supplied together with an exact package_id, the call should raise ConanException instead of accepting the query.
When code depends on ConanAPI.search or SearchAPI.recipes(), it should be considered incompatible with 2.20.0 and migrated to the supported listing API.

When a caller reads ConanAPI.home_folder, it should reflect the configured location, but attempts to change the effective home/cache by mutating that attribute after construction should not be supported.
When ConanAPI is initialized on Python 3.6 or lower, initialization should fail because Python 3.7+ is required.

task_20.title: Privatize undocumented Conan Python API members
task_20.description: Conan 2.20.0 narrows the supported Python API surface. Undocumented sub-API attributes and helper members that were previously reachable are now private or removed, callers are expected to use explicit public methods such as configuration getters, list operations, and the documented cache, upload, and download APIs, and `ConanAPI` now requires Python 3.7 or newer.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that integrations upgrading to Conan 2.20.0 use only the documented Conan Python API surface, no longer depend on undocumented sub-API attributes or helper members that were previously reachable, and initialize `ConanAPI` only on supported Python runtimes.

expectation.grounded: `ConanAPI` should expose the supported public sub-APIs such as `config`, `remotes`, `list`, `profiles`, `install`, `graph`, `export`, `remove`, `new`, `upload`, `download`, `cache`, `lockfile`, `local`, `audit`, `workspace`, and `report`, with `home_folder` exposed as a read-only property. `ConfigAPI` should provide public configuration access through `home()`, `install()`, `install_pkg()`, `get()`, `show()`, `conf_list()`, and `clean()`. Previously reachable but undocumented members, including sub-API `.conan_api` references, `ConanAPI.search`, `ConfigAPI.global_conf`, `ConfigAPI.builtin_confs`, `ConfigAPI.settings_yml`, `ConfigAPI.load_config()`, `ConfigAPI.set_core_confs()`, `ConfigAPI.reinit()`, `ListAPI.packages_configurations()`, `ListAPI.filter_packages_configurations()`, and `ListAPI.filter_packages_profile()`, should no longer be available as supported public API. Constructing `ConanAPI` should require Python 3.7 or newer and reject older runtimes with `ConanException`.
expectation.conceptual: The upgrade should make the Python API surface explicit: supported workflows must go through documented methods for configuration, listing, cache, upload, and download operations, while internal state and helper objects are no longer available for direct use. Integrations should also run only on supported Python versions.

constraints.grounded: Existing documented workflows must preserve their observable behavior through the remaining public entry points: `ConfigAPI.get()` and `show()` must still resolve effective configuration values, `ConfigAPI.install()`, `install_pkg()`, and `clean()` must still reinitialize the Conan API as needed, and the public list, cache, upload, and download methods must continue to operate against the active global configuration after reinitialization. The change should narrow public access without changing normal recipe/package resolution, cache lookup, upload, or download semantics beyond the removed undocumented members and the new Python runtime floor.
constraints.conceptual: Do not change normal supported Conan workflows. The intended incompatibilities are limited to removing unsupported internal access paths and enforcing the newer minimum Python version.

behavior: Sub-API instances now keep their parent API reference as a private `_conan_api` attribute instead of exposing a public `conan_api` attribute.

`ConfigAPI` no longer exposes public `global_conf`, `builtin_confs`, `settings_yml`, `load_config()`, `set_core_confs()`, or `reinit()` access; public configuration interaction is through methods such as `get()`, `show()`, `conf_list()`, `home()`, `install()`, `install_pkg()`, and `clean()`.
`ListAPI` no longer exposes package-configuration discovery and filtering helpers as public API; those helpers are now private methods.
`ConanAPI.search` is no longer provided on `ConanAPI`; listing logic no longer depends on a public search sub-API.
`ConanAPI.home_folder` is exposed as a read-only property that reports the resolved Conan home location.
