Constructing `ConanAPI` under Python 3.6 or older now raises `ConanException`; Python 3.7 or newer is required.
acceptance_criteria: When integration code reads configuration values, it should do so through `ConanAPI.config.get()` or `ConanAPI.config.show()` and receive the effective configuration result without needing direct access to `global_conf`.
When built-in configuration definitions are needed, `ConanAPI.config.conf_list()` should provide them, and `ConanAPI.config.builtin_confs` should not be relied on as a public member.

When client code accesses previously reachable undocumented members such as `subapi.conan_api`, `ConanAPI.search`, `ConanAPI.config.global_conf`, `ConanAPI.config.settings_yml`, `ConanAPI.config.load_config()`, `ConanAPI.config.set_core_confs()`, or `ConanAPI.list.packages_configurations()`, those members should be unavailable as public API and direct access should fail rather than remain supported.
When `ConanAPI.home_folder` is read, it should return the resolved Conan home path without requiring writable direct state on the API object.
When `ConanAPI` is constructed on Python 3.6 or older, initialization should be rejected with `ConanException`; when constructed on Python 3.7 or newer, initialization should proceed.

When supported public operations such as configuration install or clean, recipe and package revision listing, upload, download, and cache path lookup are invoked after reinitialization, they should continue to behave consistently through the documented API surface.

task_23.title: Support versioned system packages and accurate APT package detection
task_23.description: The 2.20.0 upgrade extends Conan's system package manager tooling to recognize version-qualified system package requirements and fixes APT package detection so packages are only treated as already installed when the architecture actually matches. This reduces false positives on multi-architecture systems and makes version-pinned system package requirements observable during package checks.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan's system package manager tool accepts version-qualified system package requirements and that APT only considers a package satisfied when the installed package matches the requested package architecture and, when requested, the required version.

expectation.grounded: In `conan.tools.system.package_manager`, package presence checks should evaluate the original package specification, including an optional version, rather than reducing it to name-only matching. For backends that expose version-aware checks, a version-qualified package requirement should only be considered present when the installed version matches. For `Apt`, package detection should validate the installed package architecture against the requested or resolved architecture and allow architecture-independent `all` packages. If a version is requested for a package manager that does not support version-aware checks, Conan should emit a warning and continue with the unversioned package name instead of failing.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to express a desired system package version through Conan's system package tooling, and Conan should honor that version when the underlying package manager can verify it. On APT-based systems, Conan should no longer report a package as already installed merely because the same package name exists for a different architecture.

constraints.grounded: Unversioned package requirements must continue to work. APT checks must not treat a package installed only for another architecture as satisfying the requirement; only the matching architecture or an `all` package may satisfy it. Backends without version-aware checking must preserve existing behavior apart from surfacing a warning that version pinning cannot be enforced.
constraints.conceptual: Existing non-versioned package usage should remain compatible. The fix must avoid false positives in multi-architecture environments without turning unsupported version pinning into a hard failure.

behavior: System package presence checks now evaluate package specifications that may include a requested version.
When the selected system package backend supports version-aware queries, a version-qualified package is only considered installed if the installed version matches the requested version.
APT package checks now validate the installed package architecture and accept only the matching architecture or architecture-independent `all` packages as satisfying the requirement.
APT no longer treats a package installed for a different architecture as satisfying an otherwise matching package name.
When a version is requested for a backend without version-aware checking support, Conan warns and falls back to unversioned package matching behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan consumer declares a system package requirement with a specific version and the selected package manager supports version-aware checks, Conan should report the package as present only if that exact version is installed.
When the selected package manager does not support version-aware package checks, Conan should continue processing the requirement and surface a warning that the requested version cannot be enforced.

When Conan checks an APT package in a multi-architecture environment, it should treat the package as installed only if the installed package architecture matches the requested or resolved architecture, or the package is architecture-independent.
When an APT package with the same name exists only under a different architecture, Conan should still report the requested package as missing.
When no package version is requested, Conan should preserve existing system package behavior aside from the corrected APT architecture matching.

task_24.title: Preserve runtime_deploy subfolder layout
task_24.description: The 2.20.0 update changes the runtime_deploy deployer so deployed runtime binaries and shared libraries keep their original subfolder structure instead of being flattened into one output directory. This prevents deployed relative symlinks from breaking and keeps nested runtime artifacts available at the paths consumers expect.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the runtime_deploy deployer preserves the relative subfolder structure of deployed runtime artifacts so nested libraries and binaries remain available in their original layout and deployed symlinks do not break when they reference files inside subdirectories.

expectation.grounded: When Conan installs dependencies with the runtime_deploy deployer, artifacts selected from runtime locations such as package bin and lib contents should be copied into the deployer output using their relative paths beneath those source directories instead of collapsing all files into the top-level output folder. Nested directories must therefore be reproduced in the deployed output. If tools.deployer:symlinks is enabled, deployed symlink entries should continue to resolve because their referenced targets in subfolders are also deployed at matching relative paths. If symlink deployment is disabled, symlink entries should still be omitted while regular files continue to be deployed within the preserved folder structure.
expectation.conceptual: Upgrading to 2.20.0 should make runtime_deploy mirror the dependency runtime folder layout in the deploy output. Users should be able to rely on nested runtime files and relative symlinks remaining usable after deployment, without flattening everything into a single directory.

constraints.grounded: This change should affect destination layout only for deployed runtime artifacts. runtime_deploy should continue selecting the same eligible runtime files, continue honoring whether symlink entries are deployed, and continue skipping redundant copies when the same file already exists at the same deployed relative location with identical contents.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should preserve existing runtime deployment behavior apart from keeping subfolders. It should not change which runtime artifacts are eligible for deployment or require a different deployment flow.

behavior: runtime_deploy now places each deployed runtime artifact under the output directory using its relative subfolder path from the source runtime directory instead of flattening all files into one folder.
Runtime artifacts located in nested subdirectories are deployed with those nested directories preserved.
When symlink deployment is enabled, relative symlinks deployed alongside preserved subfolders remain resolvable because their targets are available at matching relative paths in the output.
When symlink deployment is disabled, symlink entries are still skipped, while non-symlink runtime files are deployed into the preserved directory structure.
If a destination file already exists at the same relative deployed path with identical contents, runtime_deploy continues to avoid an unnecessary recopy.
acceptance_criteria: When a dependency exposes runtime files in both top-level and nested subfolders, installing with runtime_deploy should produce an output that preserves those nested subfolders instead of placing every file in one directory.
When a deployed runtime symlink refers to a file inside a subfolder and symlink deployment is enabled, the deployed symlink should remain valid from the deploy output.
When symlink deployment is not enabled, runtime_deploy should omit symlink entries but still deploy real runtime files into their corresponding preserved subfolders.
When a runtime artifact would be deployed to a relative path that already contains an identical file, runtime_deploy should leave the existing deployed file in place rather than duplicating work.

task_25.title: Adapt integrations to Conan 2.20.0 API contract changes
task_25.description: Conan 2.20.0 changes the public ConanAPI contract: search-style access moves to the list/select API, the resolved home folder becomes immutable after initialization, and the minimum supported Python runtime is raised to 3.7.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that integrations upgrading to Conan 2.20.0 stop depending on `ConanAPI.search`, treat `ConanAPI.home_folder` as read-only after initialization, and only run `ConanAPI` on supported Python versions while preserving supported package discovery and home-resolution behavior.

expectation.grounded: `ConanAPI.search` should no longer be treated as a supported public entry point. Search and selection workflows should use `ConanAPI.list.select()` and the documented list-related objects such as `ListPattern`, `PackageList`, and `MultiPackageList`. `ConanAPI.home_folder` should be exposed as a read-only property that reflects the resolved Conan user home chosen during initialization, including normal constructor, `CONAN_HOME`, and `.conanrc` resolution. Creating `ConanAPI` on Python versions below 3.7 should fail with `ConanException`.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, callers should use the list-based API for package discovery, the Conan home location should be fixed when the API instance starts instead of being reassigned later, and unsupported Python runtimes should be rejected at startup.

constraints.grounded: Do not rely on undocumented or previously public ListAPI helper methods that were reduced from the supported surface area. Do not reintroduce a writable `home_folder` attribute or depend on mutating it before `reinit()` to relocate the Conan home. Making `home_folder` read-only must not remove supported startup-time home selection through constructor input, environment configuration, or `.conanrc` resolution.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should narrow the supported public API without removing the ability to discover packages through the official list workflow, and it should harden home-folder handling without breaking supported ways of choosing the Conan home before startup.

behavior: `ConanAPI.home_folder` is now a read-only property representing the resolved Conan user home for the lifetime of the API instance.
Changing the home location by assigning to `ConanAPI.home_folder` and then calling `reinit()` is no longer a supported behavior.
`ConanAPI.search` is removed from the public API surface; selection and filtering are expected to go through `ConanAPI.list.select()`.
Conan now requires Python 3.7 or newer when initializing `ConanAPI`, and older runtimes raise `ConanException`.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer creates `ConanAPI`, it should expose the resolved home folder through `home_folder` but not allow that value to be reassigned as part of normal API use.

When a consumer needs search-like recipe or package selection after upgrading, the supported public workflow should be available through `ConanAPI.list.select()` rather than through `ConanAPI.search`.
When `reinit()` is called, it should not depend on callers mutating `home_folder` to move the Conan home to a different location.
When `ConanAPI` is initialized on Python 3.6 or older, initialization should be rejected with a `ConanException`; Python 3.7 and newer should remain valid.
